utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Today's hearing was set for the purpose of having a pre-trial conference and the opening statements in the case. It will be apparent to all of you that the accused Stanisic is not present. In that regard, I have two reports which the parties will also have. The first is from Dr. Falke, the medical officer of the Detention Unit. It's dated the 28th of March. I'll read the relevant parts. It says that: "I am to report on the medical condition of Mr. Stanisic to allow adjustments to the schedule to be made and therefore, I must inform you about the urgent hospitalisation of my patient yesterday." The 28th was Friday of last week, so the patient, Mr. Stanisic, would have been hospitalised on Thursday of last week. The report continues: "Due to the acute nature of his kidney stones, he was taken by ambulance to the accident and emergency department of the Bronovo hospital. Following thorough investigation by the urologist, Mr. Stanisic was transferred to the penitentiary hospital where he will remain and undergo a specific treatment for a period of 7 days. After this period, the urologist will reassess his situation, performing further diagnostics and treatment as necessary. Consequently, he will be unable to attend court until this acute problem is resolved." Then you will recall that the Trial Chamber had requested the registrar to have Mr. Stanisic examined by a psychiatrist, and we have a communication from Dr. de Man, who is a psychiatrist, and that is dated the -- I'm trying to find the date -- the 31st of March. And he says in his letter to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: My apologies for the interruption but is the court -- we would be greatly indebted if the court would not read out the second paragraph of Dr. de Man's letter because it contains a rather private and at the same time new element in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't consider it any longer private and new. The question of Mr. Stanisic's health has taken on an importance in this case that it is a matter of public interest, and that is why this session is being held not in private. Ordinarily, it would be, but I have made a determination, as I did previously, that the court hearing and discussion in relation to Mr. Stanisic's illness would be held in public. So I will read Dr. de Man's letter to the registrar. He says that: "The examination took place at the prison hospital where Mr. Stanisic was admitted because renal colic a day earlier. The conclusion of my examination is that the subject is suffering from major depression with psychotic features and is clearly unfit to stand trial on psychiatric grounds only. His medical status will be judged by other experts." "After consultation with the UNDU psychiatrist, Mr. Stanisic's medication was changed to a hopefully more effective tricyclic antidepressant drug. Even if this medication has a very positive result, I do not expect the subject's fitness to be restored within at least three, possibly six months. Please expect my full report with motivation shortly." I am given to understand that by 4.00 today, the registry would have received the fuller report from Dr. de Man, and we are also very eager to see that report. Now, this is the third time that this trial has been unable to commence because of Mr. Stanisic's medical condition. We can't continue in this manner. The Trial Chamber has been deliberating on this very carefully and we are of the view that certain steps will have to be considered. An important factor is that there is another accused who is on trial, and the prolonged postponement of the commencement of the trial is bound to affect his right to a fair and expeditious trial. It is the Chamber's intention to invite the parties to make submissions on the future course of the trial, and I will just outline some possibilities. I'd ask the parties to take note of the possibilities and I'll hear their submissions tomorrow. The first is perhaps the most radical, which is the possibility of a severance under Rule 82 in the interest of justice. The second is prompted by Dr. de Man's conclusion that he does not expect Mr. Stanisic's fitness to be restored within at least three, possibly six months. Of course we don't know or we would not know until we see the fuller report from Dr. de Man on what basis he arrived at that conclusion. But that would open the possibility that the -- this trial could perhaps remain in its pre-trial phase and the President would be asked to assign the Chamber another trial. The third possibility is prompted by -- again, by Dr. de Man's finding of unfitness and here again, I repeat that we don't know the criteria which he used to arrive at that conclusion, but prompted by that finding, such as it is, the Chamber could order another round of examination of the accused and have another hearing as to the accused's fitness for trial. The fourth is that when the accused returns to the UNDU, the trial could proceed by video conference link and I would specifically ask the parties to address the conditions that would apply to ensure the most efficient and the fairest manner for conducting the proceedings along those lines. The fifth, the last possibility is following on the Chamber's earlier finding that the accused was not unfit for trial, we could set next Monday, the 7th as the date for the commencement of the trial on the basis that by that time, the accused would be out of the hospital and would have returned to the UNDU. Those are the options that the Trial Chamber sees for the -- for dealing with this particular problem which is becoming a persistent one, and which I anticipate will be with us throughout the trial. I don't know whether any of the parties would wish to make any comments at this stage. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution will indeed by tomorrow have informed -- have considered the proposals by the Chamber and make full submissions. I would like to point out, I mean the Prosecution does recognise that the summary conclusions of Dr. de Man are a cause of concern. While I do not question the competency of Dr. de Man, some of the circumstances surrounding the examination and evaluation merit

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We presumably will know when we receive the report the conditions of his examination and how much time was -- he was -- he had and whether he had any difficulties conducting that examination. But what we already know is that he examined Mr. Stanisic and made a psychiatric diagnosis of him during a time that Dr. Falke describes as an acute episode of kidney stones. Having heard from doctors in the hearings here, the pain that attends such an attack, it is hard to imagine that that has had no impact on his ability to conduct an examination. So it's the Prosecution's position that it may very well be necessary to invite Dr. de Man. To come to court and answer questions regarding how the acute kidney attack may have affected his ability to properly diagnose Mr. Stanisic. Also, given the importance of the issues implicated by Dr. de Man's letter, the Prosecution is going to request an opportunity to have Dr. Mimica conduct a follow-up examination of Mr. Stanisic. It is our position that having examined Mr. Stanisic in his native tongue, able to perceive the cultural cues during the interview at a time prior to the first appearance of what Dr. de Man describes as psychotic features, that Dr. Mimica is well equipped to provide the Chamber with a reliable assessment of Mr. Stanisic's present psychiatric condition if he has the opportunity to conduct a follow-up examination. It would be my hope that we could have Dr. Mimica here early next week. We have been trying to contact him all day but he is with patients throughout the course of the day. We expect that we will be able to speak with him this evening. It is our hope that he could conduct such an examination shortly after Mr. Stanisic is discharged from the detention unit's hospital quarters and is returned to his own room at the detention unit. So it is the Prosecution's position that this week, as the Chamber has already said, explore in greater detail Dr. de Man's summary conclusions. The Prosecution is, though, asking, and we will be guided by the Chamber whether it wishes to have this in writing, we would seek to have Dr. Mimica to return to The Hague to conduct an examination so that the Court can have a full picture of Mr. Stanisic's present psychiatric state and can make the best decision regarding the future course of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I hear the submissions you have made, but of course since I've asked the parties to make submissions tomorrow on all of the points that I have raised, you would appreciate that your request may be -- may very well be overtaken or swallowed up by some of the responses that will be given but I do note it. Any submissions from Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think what Your Honour rightly pointed, the submissions of the Prosecution are in this stage for the Defence premature to respond to. We have responses but we rather wait tomorrow, tomorrow's opportunity. I simply want to point you on one issue, namely, the language issue, if you read the letter of Dr. de Man well, you may see that Dr. de Man was assisted by two native-speaking B/C/S persons so I don't think that will make his report less viable than the report of Dr. Mimica; but again, the Defence prefers to go into the submissions of today by the adequate opportunity Your Honour will offer the Defence, namely tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence for the accused Franko Simatovic will give their comments on the proposals put forth by the Chamber tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We are adjourned until 2.15 tomorrow. Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of April, 2008 at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.49 p.m.,
